title: Right derived functors form a universal delta-functor
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category with enough injectives, $\mathcal B$ an abelian category [def-sp-abelian], $v:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ a left exact additive functor and $R^nv$ ($n\ge0$) its right derived functors computed by injective resolutions [def-sp-left-exact-additive], [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. A *$\delta$-functor* from $\mathcal A$ to $\mathcal B$ (Stacks Homology, Definition 010Q) [def-weil-pbc-delta-functor] is a family $(G^n)_{n\ge0}$ of additive functors $\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ together with, for every short exact sequence $0\to A\to B\to C\to0$ of $\mathcal A$, morphisms $\delta^n_G:G^n(C)\to G^{n+1}(A)$ such that $0\to G^0(A)\to G^0(B)\to G^0(C)\xrightarrow{\delta^0_G}G^1(A)\to\cdots$ is exact and such that for every morphism of short exact sequences $(a,b,c)$ from $0\to A\to B\to C\to0$ to $0\to A'\to B'\to C'\to0$ one has $G^{n+1}(a)\circ\delta^n_G=\delta'^n_G\circ G^n(c)$; a morphism of $\delta$-functors is a family of natural transformations $t^n:G^n\to H^n$ with $t^{n+1}\circ\delta_G=\delta_H\circ t^n$; a $\delta$-functor $G$ is *universal* (Homology, Definition 010S) [def-weil-pbc-delta-functor] if for every $\delta$-functor $H$ and every natural transformation $t:G^0\to H^0$ there is a unique morphism of $\delta$-functors $(t^n)$ with $t^0=t$. Then there are morphisms $\delta^n:R^nv(C)\to R^{n+1}v(A)$, one for each short exact sequence, making $(R^nv,\delta)$ a $\delta$-functor, and this $\delta$-functor is universal; moreover $R^0v\cong v$ naturally (Stacks Derived Categories, Lemma 015B (2), (4), and Lemma 05TE; Homology, Lemma 010T: a $\delta$-functor $G$ such that for every $n>0$ and every object $A$ there is a monomorphism $A\to B$ with $G^n(A)\to G^n(B)$ zero is universal).

source.place: Lemma Tag 015B (lemma-higher-derived-functors, line 7048) items (2) and (4), whose proof of (4) cites Lemma Tag 05TE (lemma-right-derived-delta-functor); homology.tex Definitions 010Q, 010S and Lemma Tag 010T (lemma-efface-implies-universal)

proof.text: **Step 1 (the $R^nv$ are additive functors).** Every object $X$ has an injective resolution $s_X:X\to P^\bullet$ with $P^q=0$ for $q<0$ [lem-weil-pbc-left-exact-injective-resolution-degree-zero] (1). By [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-map-via-lift] each $R^nv$ is a functor $\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$, with isomorphisms $\iota^n_P:R^nv(X)\to H^n(v(P^\bullet))$ such that $R^nv(h)=(\iota^n_Q)^{-1}H^n(v(\varphi))\iota^n_P$ for every morphism $h:X\to Y$, resolution $s_Y:Y\to Q^\bullet$ and morphism of complexes $\varphi:P^\bullet\to Q^\bullet$ with $\varphi^0s_X=s_Yh$; such a $\varphi$ exists by [lem-weil-pbc-injective-resolution-lift-exists]. Additivity: for $h,h':X\to Y$ with lifts $\varphi,\varphi'$, the sum $\varphi+\varphi'$ is a morphism of complexes with $(\varphi^0+\varphi'^0)s_X=s_Y(h+h')$, so it lifts $h+h'$; $v$ is additive [def-sp-left-exact-additive], so $v(\varphi+\varphi')=v(\varphi)+v(\varphi')$ termwise, and $H^n$ is additive on morphisms of complexes (it is induced on subquotients); hence $R^nv(h+h')=R^nv(h)+R^nv(h')$.

source.place: Definition Tag 015A (definition-higher-derived-functors: R^iF = H^i o RF, a composite of additive functors) and Lemma Tag 013P (lemma-morphisms-lift) for the lifts; Lemma Tag 015B (lemma-higher-derived-functors), whose (1)-(4) presuppose the functors R^iF

proof.text: **Step 2 ($R^0v\cong v$ naturally).** For each $X$ fix a resolution $s_X:X\to P_X^\bullet$ as in Step 1. Since $v$ is left exact, [lem-weil-pbc-left-exact-injective-resolution-degree-zero] (2) gives an isomorphism $\eta_X:v(X)\to H^0(v(P_X^\bullet))=\ker v(d^0)$, the factorization of $v(s_X)$ through $\ker v(d^0)\subset v(P_X^0)$. Put $\epsilon_X=(\iota^0_{P_X})^{-1}\eta_X:v(X)\xrightarrow{\sim}R^0v(X)$. Naturality: for $h:X\to Y$ choose a lift $\varphi$ [lem-weil-pbc-injective-resolution-lift-exists]; $H^0(v\varphi)$ is the restriction of $v(\varphi^0)$ to the kernels, and $v(\varphi^0)v(s_X)=v(\varphi^0s_X)=v(s_Yh)=v(s_Y)v(h)$, so after composing with the monomorphism $\ker v(d^0_Q)\hookrightarrow v(Q^0)$ one gets $H^0(v\varphi)\eta_X=\eta_Yv(h)$; with $R^0v(h)=(\iota^0_{P_Y})^{-1}H^0(v\varphi)\iota^0_{P_X}$ [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-map-via-lift] this is $R^0v(h)\epsilon_X=\epsilon_Yv(h)$. So $\epsilon:v\to R^0v$ is a natural isomorphism.

source.place: Lemma Tag 015B (lemma-higher-derived-functors) part (2), which is Lemma Tag 05TD (lemma-left-exact-higher-derived) part (3) and its proof: for 0 -> A -> K^0 -> K^1 exact, F left exact gives F(A) = H^0(F(K))

proof.text: **Step 3 (the distinguished triangle of a short exact sequence).** Let $0\to A\xrightarrow{f}B\xrightarrow{g}C\to0$ be short exact in $\mathcal A$. The complexes $A[0],B[0],C[0]$ concentrated in degree $0$ with the morphisms $f[0],g[0]$ form a sequence of complexes which is short exact in every degree (the given sequence in degree $0$, zero elsewhere), i.e. a short exact sequence of complexes [lem-weil-pbc-cochain-complexes-degreewise-exact] (2). By [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-triangle] there is $w_{A\to B\to C}:C[0]\to A[0][1]$ in $D(\mathcal A)$ such that $T_{A\to B\to C}=(A[0]\xrightarrow{f}B[0]\xrightarrow{g}C[0]\xrightarrow{w}A[0][1])$ is distinguished, and for a morphism $(a,b,c)$ of short exact sequences $(a[0],b[0],c[0])$ is a morphism of short exact sequences of complexes, so $(a,b,c)$ (images under $Q$) is a morphism of triangles $T_{A\to B\to C}\to T_{A'\to B'\to C'}$ [def-weil-pbc-triangles-with-shift]: $a[1]\circ w=w'\circ c$. All three vertices have cohomology only in degree $0$, so they lie in $D^+(\mathcal A)$, a full triangulated subcategory [def-weil-pbc-bounded-derived-subcategories]; $T$ is a distinguished triangle there.

source.place: Lemma Tag 05TE (lemma-right-derived-delta-functor), proof: 'The functor A -> Comp^+(A), A |-> A[0] is exact. The functor Comp^+(A) -> D^+(A) is a delta-functor, see Lemma 0152 (lemma-derived-canonical-delta-functor)'

proof.text: **Step 4 (apply $Rv$).** Let $Rv:D^+(\mathcal A)\to D^+(\mathcal B)$ be the right derived functor of $v$ with its shift isomorphism $\sigma$; by [lem-weil-pbc-derived-direct-image-triangulated] it is a triangulated functor, so $Rv(T)=(Rv(A[0])\xrightarrow{Rv f}Rv(B[0])\xrightarrow{Rv g}Rv(C[0])\xrightarrow{\sigma_{A[0]}\circ Rv(w)}Rv(A[0])[1])$ is distinguished in $D^+(\mathcal B)$, hence in $D(\mathcal B)$. For a morphism $(a,b,c)$ of short exact sequences, $(Rv\,a,Rv\,b,Rv\,c)$ is a morphism of triangles $Rv(T)\to Rv(T')$ [def-weil-pbc-triangles-with-shift]: the first two squares commute by functoriality of $Rv$, and the third by Step 3 and naturality of $\sigma$: $\sigma_{A'[0]}Rv(w')Rv(c)=\sigma_{A'[0]}Rv(a[1])Rv(w)=(Rv\,a)[1]\sigma_{A[0]}Rv(w)$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 05TE, proof: 'The functor RF : D^+(A) -> D^+(B) is exact'; Lemma Tag 0159 (lemma-right-derived-properties) parts (1), (3), (4); Lemma Tag 05TI (lemma-enough-injectives-right-derived): RF everywhere defined

proof.text: **Step 5 (the connecting maps and the long exact sequence).** Apply the long exact cohomology sequence of a distinguished triangle of $D(\mathcal B)$ [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact], with connecting maps $\partial^n:H^n(Rv(C[0]))\to H^{n+1}(Rv(A[0]))$ induced by the third morphism $\sigma_{A[0]}Rv(w)$ through $H^{n+1}(X)=H^n(X[1])$ as in [lem-weil-pbc-derived-cohomology-ladder], to $Rv(T)$: the sequence $\cdots\to H^n(Rv(A[0]))\to H^n(Rv(B[0]))\to H^n(Rv(C[0]))\xrightarrow{\partial^n}H^{n+1}(Rv(A[0]))\to\cdots$ is exact. By [lem-sp-derived-functor-single-identification] there are isomorphisms $\theta^n_X:H^n(Rv(X[0]))\to R^nv(X)$, $n\ge0$, natural in $X$; naturality for $f$ and $g$ gives $\theta^n_BH^n(Rv f)=R^nv(f)\theta^n_A$ and $\theta^n_CH^n(Rv g)=R^nv(g)\theta^n_B$. Define $\delta^n_{A\to B\to C}:=\theta^{n+1}_A\circ\partial^n\circ(\theta^n_C)^{-1}:R^nv(C)\to R^{n+1}v(A)$. The $\theta$'s then form an isomorphism from the part in degrees $\ge0$ of the exact sequence above to $R^0v(A)\to R^0v(B)\to R^0v(C)\xrightarrow{\delta^0}R^1v(A)\to\cdots\xrightarrow{\delta^n}R^{n+1}v(A)\to\cdots$, so the latter is exact at every term from $R^0v(B)$ on (exactness at a term is preserved by an isomorphism of sequences).

source.place: Lemma Tag 05TE (1), proof: 'the functor H^0 : D^+(B) -> B is a homological functor ... Hence we get the structure of a delta-functor from Lemma 05SR (lemma-compose-delta-functor-homological) and Lemma 0151 (lemma-exact-compose-delta-functor)'; Lemma Tag 015B (1) and Definition Tag 015A (R^iF = H^i o RF)

proof.text: **Step 6 (the start $0\to R^0v(A)\to R^0v(B)$).** By Step 2, $R^0v(f)=\epsilon_Bv(f)\epsilon_A^{-1}$. As $f$ is a kernel of $g$ and $v$ is left exact (preserves kernels) [def-sp-left-exact-additive], $v(f)$ is a kernel of $v(g)$, in particular a monomorphism; hence $R^0v(f)$ is a monomorphism and the sequence of Step 5 preceded by $0$ is exact.

source.place: Lemma Tag 05TD (lemma-left-exact-higher-derived) proof of (2): 0 -> R^0F(A) -> R^0F(B) -> R^0F(C) is exact; Homology Definition 010Q axiom (1)

proof.text: **Step 7 (naturality of $\delta$).** Let $(a,b,c)$ be a morphism from $0\to A\to B\to C\to0$ to $0\to A'\to B'\to C'\to0$. By Step 4, $(Rv\,a,Rv\,b,Rv\,c)$ is a morphism of distinguished triangles $Rv(T)\to Rv(T')$, so by [lem-weil-pbc-derived-cohomology-ladder] $H^{n+1}(Rv\,a)\circ\partial^n=\partial'^n\circ H^n(Rv\,c)$. Naturality of $\theta$ [lem-sp-derived-functor-single-identification] for $a$ (degree $n+1$) and $c$ (degree $n$) turns this into $R^{n+1}v(a)\circ\delta^n_{A\to B\to C}=\delta^n_{A'\to B'\to C'}\circ R^nv(c)$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 05TE (1) (the delta-functor structure includes compatibility with morphisms of short exact sequences, Homology Definition 010Q (2)); Lemma Tag 0152 (functoriality of the triangle)

proof.text: **Step 8 ($\delta$-functor).** By Step 1 the $R^nv$ are additive functors; Steps 5 and 6 give axiom (1) and Step 7 axiom (2) of a $\delta$-functor [def-weil-pbc-delta-functor]. So $(R^nv,\delta)_{n\ge0}$ is a $\delta$-functor from $\mathcal A$ to $\mathcal B$.

**Step 9 (effaceability).** Let $n>0$ and $A\in\mathcal A$. As $\mathcal A$ has enough injectives there is a monomorphism $u:A\to I$ with $I$ injective [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. By [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-injective-vanishing] $R^nv(I)=0$, so $R^nv(u):R^nv(A)\to R^nv(I)=0$ is the zero morphism.

source.place: Lemma Tag 015B part (3) ('injective objects are acyclic'); Lemma Tag 05TE (2) hypothesis 'every object is a subobject of a right acyclic object', with Lemma Tag 015C (lemma-F-acyclic) giving R^iF(I)=0 for i>0 on acyclics

proof.text: **Step 10 (universality).** By Steps 8 and 9 the $\delta$-functor $(R^nv,\delta)$ satisfies the hypothesis of [lem-weil-pbc-effaceable-delta-functor-universal] (for every $n>0$ and every $A$ a monomorphism $u$ with $R^nv(u)=0$), hence it is universal. Together with Step 2 ($R^0v\cong v$) this proves the statement.

source.place: Lemma Tag 05TE part (2), proof: 'Part (2) follows from Homology, Lemma 010T (lemma-efface-implies-universal) and the description of acyclics in Lemma 015C'; Lemma Tag 015B part (4)

split_report.summary: Checked every tag in derived.tex/homology.tex: 015B = lemma-higher-derived-functors (items (2) R^0F=F via 05TD, (3) injectives acyclic, (4) universal delta-functor via 05TE), 05TE = lemma-right-derived-delta-functor, 010Q/010R/010S/010T as cited; the statement's citations are correct (only the def node of delta-functors was added to it). Split along Stacks' own route (05TE), not the horseshoe: delta^n is H^n of R v applied to the triangle A[0]->B[0]->C[0]->A[0][1] of Lemma 0152, transported by the natural iso H^n(Rv(X[0])) = R^nv(X); exactness and naturality then come from the long exact sequence of a triangle and its ladder, with no independence-of-resolution argument needed. Ten steps: additivity of R^nv (map-via-lift + new Mathlib leaf lem-weil-pbc-injective-resolution-lift-exists, Stacks 013P(2), InjectiveResolution.desc); R^0v = v naturally (leaf degree-zero node + lifts); triangle (leaves complex-ses-triangle, degreewise-exact; D^+ subcategory); Rv triangulated (closed node lem-weil-pbc-derived-direct-image-triangulated); LES and delta (leaf lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact, leaf ladder, closed lem-sp-derived-functor-single-identification); start of the sequence (left exactness, elementary); naturality (ladder); delta-functor (elementary); effaceability (leaf injective-vanishing); universality (new unsplit lem-weil-pbc-effaceable-delta-functor-universal, Homology 010T). New def node def-weil-pbc-delta-functor (010Q-010S, unsplit, not in Mathlib). Mathlib: no delta-functors, no long exact sequence for Functor.rightDerived (rightDerivedFunctorPlus not yet triangulated, TODO in Mathlib). The source repository has the sorry-free CategoryTheory.ShortComplex.ShortExact.exists_rightDerived_delta_exact (exactness at R^qF(C) and R^{q+1}F(A) only, existential delta, no naturality): a partial cover by the same route, not attached.
